evidence.quote: The byway continues east to Nutt, paralleling a spur line of the Atchison, Topeka, and Santa Fe Railroad, built in 1884 to transport supplies into Lake Valley and ore out.

evidence.claim: Miners called it the bridal chamber, and it yielded 2.5 million troy ounces of silver.
evidence.quote: a silver-lined cavity they named the "bridal chamber" that alone yielded 2.5 million troy ounces (78 tonnes) of silver.

evidence.claim: Nutt began as a place to transfer a journey from rail to wagon.
evidence.quote: Wagon trains left Nutt for the mining communities in the Black Range until the Santa Fe ran a spur line up to Lake Valley in 1884.

evidence.claim: Founded in 1881 as a Santa Fe depot and water station, it sent wagon trains toward the Black Range mining communities.
evidence.quote: The town of Nutt was founded in 1881 as a depot and water station on the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railway

evidence.claim: The railroad’s Lake Valley spur arrived in 1884, and Nutt quickly declined afterward.
evidence.quote: After the spur was built, Nutt quickly declined.

evidence.claim: Its post office closed that year, reopened in 1899 and lasted until 1939.
evidence.quote: Nutt had a post office from 1881 until 1884, and again from 1899 until 1939.

evidence.claim: The settlement occupies a rise between Los Uvas Valley and Macho Creek Valley, a pass through remnants of the Good Sight Mountains.
evidence.quote: Nutt is located on a rise between Los Uvas Valley to the east, and the Macho Creek Valley to the west.  The rise is actually a pass through the remnants of the Good Sight Mountains

evidence.claim: South of Hillsboro, the highway crosses Oak Spring, Tierra Blanca and Berrenda creeks before reaching Lake Valley; farther south it passes between the Nutt and Round Mountains.
evidence.quote: At 17.3 miles the road crosses Berrenda Creek with a few agricultural fields in the vicinity. Shortly after, the road passes by North and South Sibley Mountains named after a confederate general Henry H. Sibley. After passing a 22-mile mark, the highway crosses the Tierra Blanca Creek, and at 23.5 miles Oak Spring Creek.

evidence.claim: farther south it passes between the Nutt and Round Mountains.
evidence.quote: The road passes through the Chihuahuan grasslands between the Nutt and Round Mountains.

evidence.claim: The town’s name began as Hillsborough, chosen by prospectors in December 1877, before being shortened to Hillsboro.
evidence.quote: The town was named Hillsborough by prospectors in December 1877, but later shortened to Hillsboro.

evidence.claim: The mining began after a rancher found silver deposits in 1876 and sold his claims to an engineer two years later.
evidence.quote: A rancher found the Lake Valley silver deposits in Sierra County in 1876. Two years later he sold his claims to an engineer, who began mining.

evidence.claim: Nutt Mountain, north of the settlement, is a volcanic plug made of layered rhyolites and has also been called Sunday Cone.
evidence.quote: Nutt Mountain is a volcanic plug composed of layered rhyolites, and has also been called Sunday Cone.

evidence.claim: Nutt Mountain, north of the settlement
evidence.quote: Nutt Mountain at 5,940 ft., is 2.5 miles north of Nutt.

flags: The NMDOT cache is truncated JSON, but its Lake Valley records explicitly identify NM 27, NM 152 and both designations. No designation date is supported.

The cache supplies little road engineering or travel-time detail and does not establish the outer endpoint of the NM 152 section; the driving narrative identifies that section without inventing an endpoint.
Current Lake Valley access restrictions appear only in Wikipedia, not a cached site-manager page. Daylight-only access and weekly closure details are omitted pending manager verification.
No current factual claim was dropped for lack of cache support. The Nutt robbery and nickname were omitted for focus, not because they are absent from the cache.
